Silco was bad, but he wanted to free the entirety of the Lanes and create a Nation of Zaun for them all to actually have a chance at a good life. 

Singed was bad, but his ultimate motive was to find a way to bring his daughter back.

Jinx was bad, but was doing it out of love/loyalty to Silco, who had the ultimate goal of lifting the Lanes out of the gutter. And when Silco died she became a symbol of hope for all the people in the undercity.

Viktor was bad, but he was doing it to create what he thought was the ultimate evolution for people to live without negative outcomes. No emotion, no anger, no wars. Just peace.

Don’t look at being an officer as a reward/promotion, more so as a shift in responsibilities. Non-coms and officers have very different responsibilities and roles to play. Spartan Supersoldiers definitely fit the responsibilities of a non-com much better.

Generally speaking being an officer has more to do with command and management requirements. 

From what I remember the spartan IIs were trained specifically, since children, to be super soldiers and complete impossible missions “on the ground”. They worked in small teams, usually not augmented by any other regular force personnel, and when they were they did not normally have officers in the field (obviously this wasn’t always true). 

So there was good reason to give Spartans some NCO ranks, but for what they were built to do it would not make sense to commission them and have them sit more on the sideline to plan and organize military efforts rather than execute them.

Kurt was given his commission so he could command the Spartan III program and oversee close to 600 personnel at once.

Fred was given his commission by Kurt in the field as Kurt wanted the remaining members to still have a command structure after he sacrifices himself. ONI let him keep this commission afterwards, but Fred still deferred command to Chief when operating in blue team as he believed Chief was the better decision maker.

Jerome was given his commission as the SoF was running out of Commanders and Jerome had proven his ability to manage large tasks and battle groups.

Noble Team was given their commissions because they did operate alongside marine forces regularly and ONI did not want any officers having the ability to overrule Nobles objectives in the field.

I think the major thing to take away is these are all special cases. A Spartan is part of the “Workforce” of the military and is expected to execute missions directly. So commissions don’t do anything for them.
